name: seattle-skyline
note: the default view: low oblique across elliott bay at the downtown towers. dense fine tiles, lots of vertical geometry

name: rainier-oblique
note: big terrain relief at distance — exercises the horizon far plane and coarse-tile lod out to the skyline

name: grand-canyon-low
note: low over strong relief: the case where terrain-hug and the ground column matter, and where seam cracks show up worst

name: manhattan-down
note: steep look-down on dense urban mesh — heavy fine-tile counts, good draw-submission load

name: globe-high
note: orbital altitude: coarse levels only, and the altitude/2 near plane branch

name: alps-ortho
note: orthographic projection over mountains — the separate ortho extent/clip path

name: seattle-jpg
note: same view as seattle-skyline but with ?jpg — forces texture_s3tc_supported=false, so this is the no-s3tc jpeg texture path (rocktree_gl renderInit). no browser here lacks s3tc, so this flag is the only way that branch runs

name: seattle-tunnel
note: tunnel mode over downtown seattle, 3 km around (r 480 m), camera 120 m up looking level: the ground ahead curls up in front of the camera and the seam is level behind it. exercises the rect-driven selection with a rect that moves with the camera, the wrapped-range offset, and the continuous ground measurement

name: tunnel-lake-edge
note: a small tunnel (1.3 km around) hugging the ground beside lake union, looking a little up: the lake's coarse tile used to come through the roll as a navy slab across half the frame (a triangle that spans a large arc, clipped straight across); the tunnel now leaves a hole until the fine tile lands. the regression case for that
